newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil orders Antarctica-Anheuser to undo venture.
newsitem.headline: Brazil orders Antarctica-Anheuser to undo venture.

text.p: A Brazilian anti-trust body on Wednesday ordered brewers Antarctica and U.S.-based Anheuser-Busch Cos Inc, maker of Budweiser beer, to dissolve their joint-venture within two years, an official said.

The ruling, however, has not been formalized yet as it hinges on the vote of one member of the government's Administrative Economic Defence Council (Cade) who requested more information on the case, he said.
"A final decision was not formalized. But it is very unlikely that the ruling will change," he said. The member who requested information has until July 2 to announce his vote.
Five members of the council ruled against the venture set up in 1995, the official said.

Anheuser-Busch and local brewery Companhia Antarctica Paulista created the joint-venture to distribute Budweiser in Brazil. Under the deal, Anheuser, the world's largest brewer, also bought an equity stake in the Brazilian company.
The decision was the same taken by Cade last week on the partnership between Brazil's Brahma and U.S. Miller Brewing Co.
But the official said the reasons that led the Cade to rule against the Anheuser-Antarctica deal were slightly different "in operational and economic terms." He did not elaborate.

The council ordered Brahma, the largest brewer in South America, and Miller to undo their joint-venture within 24 months because it was found that the partnership was against the interests of competition.

Under the venture, which had been due to expire in 2010, Brahma sold and distributed Miller products in Brazil, giving its parent company Philip Morris Cos Inc. a foothold in the booming Brazilian beer market.
The Cade found that Miller could have entered the Brazilian market on its own.

Carlos Francisco de Magalhaes, a lawyer for Antarctica, told private InvestNews agency the company will wait for the Cade's final ruling. He also said Antarctica would appeal the decision if the ruling against the venture is formalized.
